actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

device.name: UR5 unscrewing Gym environment over ROS/Gazebo

facts.text: The package registers the Gym environment id gym_unscrewing_env-v0 with entry point rl_gym.envs:UnscrewingEnv
rl_gym.envs imports UnscrewingEnv from rl_gym.envs.unscrewing_env
UnscrewingEnv subclasses gym.Env
The constructor initializes the anonymous ROS node Env_setup_node, creates a std_msgs/Int8 publisher on /action_move, and creates a Trigger service proxy for /reset_robot
The constructor sets boundaries x_low 0.478915, x_high 0.521085, y_low -0.021225, y_high 0.021225, z_low 0.02 and z_high 0.04
The action space is spaces.Discrete(7), commented as x+, x-, y+, y-, z+, z-, unscrewing
The constructor calls _seed(), which seeds self.np_random through gym.utils.seeding

step waits for a /curr_pose geometry_msgs/PoseStamped message with timeout 10, calling rospy.sleep(10) and retrying after each failure, publishes the action with action_pub, calls rospy.sleep(0.25) (the comment says a delay of 0.5s is needed), reads the state with get_state(current_pose, 0) and passes the pose read before publishing to is_done
When the episode is not done, step sets screw_touch_state when state['z'] < 0.0295 and gives reward 2 when state['force_z'] < 0 and the action is 6, otherwise reward 0
When the episode is done, step gives reward -10 if out_of_bounds(current_pose) is True, otherwise 30 + 3000 * z after a screw touch or 10 + 1.5 / z without one
step returns the legacy four-tuple (state, reward, done, {})
out_of_bounds returns True when the pose is within 0.0001 of a boundary or beyond it: x above x_high - 0.0001, x below x_low + 0.0001, and the same margin for y and z

get_state reads /curr_pose (when pos_state is 0), /FTsensor_topic (geometry_msgs/WrenchStamped, using wrench.force.z) and /screw_joint_value (std_msgs/Float32, using data), each with timeout 1 inside a loop that retries until a message arrives, and discretises the five values
discretise_data rounds x, y and z to four decimals, force_z to one decimal and screw_joint_value to three decimals
is_done is True when force_z is less than -10 or out_of_bounds(current_pose) is True for the pose it is given

reset clears screw_touch_state, calls the /reset_robot Trigger service until a call raises no exception (rospy.sleep(10) after each failure) without reading the response's success field, sleeps 1 s, waits for /curr_pose with timeout 1 and calls rospy.sleep(10000) after each failed wait, and returns get_state(current_pose, 0)
planning_script's move_action adds or subtracts step_size 0.0005 to the x, y or z of group.get_current_pose() for actions 0 to 5 (0/1 x, 2/3 y, 4/5 z) and calls move
planning_script's move sets the pose target, plans and executes with group.go(wait=True) without reading its result
planning_script uses the MoveGroupCommander arm and subscribes move_action to action_move (std_msgs/Int8)
screw_control's move_action adds step_size -0.25 to the first value of group.get_current_joint_values() for action 6 and calls move
The /curr_pose publisher publishes group.get_current_pose() as geometry_msgs/PoseStamped in a loop without a sleep, printing each pose
The /screw_joint_value publisher publishes the first value of group.get_current_joint_values() as std_msgs/Float32 in a loop without a sleep
The Gazebo FT sensor plugin publishes on FTsensor_topic at updateRate 100.0 with gaussianNoise 0.0 for the ft_sensor_drill_joint
RobotReset uses the MoveGroupCommander arm, creates service proxies for /gazebo/reset_world, /gazebo/reset_simulation and /gazebo/unpause_physics, and advertises reset_robot as a Trigger service

The reset_robot handler sets a fixed joint target, plans, executes with group.go(wait=True) without reading its result, sleeps 0.1 s, calls reset_world_srv and returns [True, 'succeded resetting the robot.']
rl_world.launch starts gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with paused defaulting to false, spawns the arm_controller and screw_controller and starts reset_robot.py
moveit_planning_execution.launch starts current_pose_publisher.py, planning_script.py, screw_control.py and current_screw_joint_publisher.py
The MoveIt controller list of rl_moveit_config names arm_controller and screw_controller with action namespace follow_joint_trajectory
The vendored ur_driver package describes itself as a driver for the UR5/10 arm based on the Polyscope control scheme
ur_driver creates an actionlib ActionServer named follow_joint_trajectory for FollowJointTrajectoryAction
Screwdriver.ino subscribes to std_msgs/Int8 on screwdriver and writes 255 to pin 9 for a value above 1, otherwise 0
The README installation instructions target ROS Kinetic and gym ==0.10.5 and launch the Gazebo world, the MoveIt planning execution and the example script

determinism.notes: the fake's transition is fixed Python arithmetic with no random source; the bridge's seed endpoint records a seed for the next reset, but the upstream reset has no seed parameter and the environment's seeded np_random generator is never used, so the seed has no effect on either the fake or the served environment

fidelity.engine: analytic:legacy-gym UR5 unscrewing stand-in (no Gazebo, MoveIt or ROS)
gaps: the fake is a pure-Python analytic stand-in: it loads no ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt, UR5 model, controller, force sensor, plugin, contact physics or wall-clock loop, and it models no dynamics

the upstream environment is a ROS client: the constructor calls rospy.init_node and creates the /action_move publisher and /reset_robot service proxy, step waits on /curr_pose and publishes the action, get_state waits on /curr_pose, /FTsensor_topic and /screw_joint_value, and reset calls the Trigger service (rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:21-32, 72-88, 171-224, 247-286); the fake performs none of these ROS operations

the upstream step has unbounded retry loops: /curr_pose is waited for with a 10 s timeout and then a 10 s sleep, /FTsensor_topic and /screw_joint_value have 1 s timeouts inside while loops, and reset retries the service forever (rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:74-79, 190-215, 261-283); the fake returns immediately

timestep_ms is 0 because the environment declares no physics timestep: the 0.25 s rospy.sleep after publishing is a ROS-time wait (simulated time when use_sim_time is set), not a simulated step, while the upstream comment says MoveIt needs 0.5 s (rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:84-85) and the MoveIt subscriber executes with go(wait=True), so the next state can be read before the motion ends; the Gazebo physics period is not declared in the clone

the fake's start pose, force values and screw-joint value are placeholders; the pose increments copy the MoveIt step sizes 0.0005 m and -0.25 rad as test data, not as limits, and the force model is a placeholder counter, not a contact or wrench model

the fake follows the upstream terminal rules (force_z < -10 or the previous pose out of bounds, rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:227-244) and reward rules (:93-113), but the previous-pose lag and the force-dependent outcome cannot match the unrun Gazebo scene

the real simulator path gym.make('gym_unscrewing_env-v0') was not run: it needs ROS 1 Kinetic, Gazebo, MoveIt, the workspace packages and gym==0.10.5 (rl_unscrew/README.md:14-43), none of which exists where the gate runs or is installed by this package
the seed endpoint is accepted and recorded for the next reset but does not change the deterministic fake or the upstream reset, which always calls the reset service
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment has no get_state/set_state checkpoint protocol, and its get_state method only reads ROS topics
no upstream simulator, ROS graph or hardware was contacted; the package is contract-checked on the fake only and makes no live-run or hardware claim

a reset proves nothing upstream: reset never reads the Trigger response's success, and the reset_robot handler returns success unconditionally after a go(wait=True) whose result it ignores (rl_unscrew/rl_gazebo_sim/srv/reset_robot.py:105-119); a failed /curr_pose wait in reset sleeps 10000 s (rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:276-283)

live construction in the server process would call the global rospy.init_node, and step, reset and get_state print progress and error lines to standard output (rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:79, 195-215, 257-283), which would corrupt an MHS server speaking over stdio

the clone also ships a real-robot path that this package does not cover: the vendored ROS-Industrial ur_driver serves follow_joint_trajectory for a real UR arm, visual-pushing-grasping/robot.py drives a real UR5 over TCP sockets, and Screwdriver.ino switches a real screwdriver on the screwdriver topic; as shipped the environment's MoveIt configuration sends trajectories to the Gazebo arm_controller and screw_controller, so only a remap would move a real arm

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: Software latch only: the runtime refuses every step, reset and seed until mhs.safety.reset and the fake stops advancing with its last observation readable; nothing upstream is called, so a live Gazebo world, which this package never drives and rl_world.launch starts unpaused, keeps running, and MoveIt still plans and executes an action already published on /action_move with go(wait=True), which nothing cancels
